slot.brief: Two bodies with equal kinetic energies (or equal momenta) but different masses; find the ratio of their momenta (or kinetic energies) using p = √(2mK).

stem: Two bodies of masses $3\ \text{kg}$ and $12\ \text{kg}$ have equal kinetic energies. The ratio of the momentum of the heavier body to that of the lighter body is

verdicts.working: For equal kinetic energy, p = √(2mK), so p₁₂/p₃ = √(12/3) = 2.

working:
$p=\sqrt{2mK}$
$$\dfrac{p_{12}}{p_3}=\sqrt{\dfrac{12}{3}}=2$$
Ratio $=2:1$.

Independent check: For equal kinetic energy, p = √(2mK), so p₁₂/p₃ = √(12/3) = 2.
solution:
For equal kinetic energy, $p=\sqrt{2mK}$; hence momentum is proportional to $\sqrt{m}$.
$$\frac{p_{12}}{p_3}=\sqrt{\frac{12}{3}}=2$$
Thus, the ratio is $2:1$.
